name: GL 00 Control (Ghost Fracture)
desc: Byte-identical Ghost Fracture. Your reference — everything else changes ONE thing vs this.

name: GL 01 Metal LOW (~150)
desc: PILLAR 1 TEST: metal dropped to the level our newer finishes use. If the purple stops jumping through, near-max metal is the body-color engine.

name: GL 02 Metal MID (~185)
desc: Pillar 1 dose-response: halfway. Tells us the metal threshold where color-jump starts dying.

name: GL 03 Rough PASTEL (150-200)
desc: PILLAR 2 TEST + the pastel doctrine on-track: roughness raised to the light-pastel band. If flashes go soft/hazy, low roughness is what makes them EXPLODE.

name: GL 04 Rough MIRROR (30-60)
desc: Pillar 2 the other direction: glossier than GF. Do flashes get even sharper/harder?

name: GL 05 Clearcoat FLAT (no cells)
desc: PILLAR 3 TEST: same metal+gloss but the carve is GONE (CC uniform 212). If gold still flashes but with no cell pattern, the carve is only the SHAPE; if gold dies, the carve is the engine.

name: GL 06 Clearcoat SHALLOW carve
desc: Pillar 3 dose-response: carve amplitude halved. How much swing does the two-color travel need?

name: GL 07 Clearcoat INVERTED
desc: Cells swap polarity (carved becomes flooded). Should swap WHERE gold vs teal appears — confirms the cells choose which env color shows.

name: GL 08 Cells MICRO (3x smaller)
desc: Structure scale: same recipe, 3x finer cells. Does fine structure shimmer instead of detonate?

name: GL 09 Cells MACRO (3x bigger)
desc: Structure scale: 3x bigger cells. Do big panels flash harder but read blocky?

name: GL 10 Full PASTEL recipe
desc: The round-5 pastel doctrine applied to GF geometry (rough 150-170, compressed carve 191-240). Head-to-head vs GL 00 settles whether pastel beats the original on track.

name: GL 11 Clearcoat MAX carve
desc: Carve amplitude pushed to the rails (cells swing 40<->250). Is more swing more magic, or does it clip into noise?
